explanation: Fires on the adverb-forming suffix token (-ly, -ily, -ically, -ously, -ately, -fully, Portuguese -amente) when it attaches to an adjective stem split into a separate token, especially descriptive manner adverbs (benignly, seductively, nastily). Whole-word adverbs like ' reasonably', ' commonly' or ' fully' fire only moderately, and non-adverb tokens barely fire.

Fires on colon tokens that separate tightly bound fields: times (03:13, 12:45), timestamps, case and docket numbers (1:08-CV), URIs, and math maps like f: X -> Y. Ordinary prose colons ('Italian: ...', 'said:') and semicolons fire only weakly.

Fires on the first token (often a single capital letter or the first subword) of a proper name, such as an organization, place, band, or person, especially when the name is broken into several tokens (L|'Orchestra, D|.C., L|UBBOCK, R|AILROAD). Later subword pieces of a name fire moderately, and ordinary words do not fire.

Fires on word-initial 'pro'-type subword fragments that start a longer word, especially medical/Latinate words: proph(ylaxis/etic), prost(hesis/aglandin), prof(anity/use/icient), prox(imate). The strongest single case was a name fragment (Pro|ff|itt). Whole common words like 'proof' or 'Professors' fire weakly.

Fires on mid-word subword continuations of words that are split into pieces, mostly foreign-language words and proper names (Finnish 'use|an', Córd|oba, Noid|a, Rhi|anna, Klaip|eda), plus some split adverb suffixes. It is a diffuse 'inside a fragmented rare word' detector with no clear semantic focus.

Fires on the content word of an idiomatic multiword phrase or phrasal verb, right after the subject or clause start: 'along (with)', '(arising/coming) out (of)', '(at the) end (of)', '(been) looking (for)', 'What say you'. Common verbs in fixed collocations ('distributed in the hope', 'We feel') fire moderately.

Fires on negation tokens: ' not', especially after modals or 'do' ('you may not use this file', 'Do not', 'Hast thou not'), plus ' without' in 'WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without', '!' in build tags, and 'no'. License boilerplate is the strongest context; sentence-initial 'Not' or 'no' fires moderately.

Fires on 'considered' (and synonyms 'deemed', 'regarded as', 'seen as') in passive or evaluative 'X is considered (to be) Y' constructions. Naming verbs ('called', 'known as', 'referred to as', 'classified as') fire moderately, and the article that follows such a verb fires weakly.

Fires on the head or final token of a company or organization name, or of a noun denoting a company ('Kel|logg', 'Oxford Instruments', 'Amicus Ther|apeutics', 'The autom|aker', 'K|ering', 'the company'). Weaker hits are domain-modifier nouns in compound terms (dental school, pulmonary disease, plant isotopes) and generic subject nouns.

Fires on mid-word subword fragments inside technical identifiers, acronyms, code tokens, and abbreviations (Daff|od|ils, os|md|roid, sc|id, e|.g, N|UL|L, C|DF, X-UA, the year digit after 'Copyright '). It has no single semantic theme beyond 'continuation inside an odd token string'.

A mixture of strong hits on function words in fixed grammatical frames: ' to' after 'possible'/'need'/'wishing', ' which' in 'by which', ' the' in 'Licensed to the', ' que' in 'parce que', and commas inside numbers or years. The top case 'on the edge' is unrelated to the rest.

Fires on the word that completes a common fixed phrase or collocation, where the next word is highly predictable: 'little is known', 'more information', 'long way', 'Nice to', 'officials said', 'at least', 'a lot more', 'not having (any luck)'. It is broadly about predictable phrase-internal function or content words, with no single lexical item.

Fires on the token ' out', as a standalone particle ('out of', 'out there', 'out and about') or as a prefix of a compound (outsource, outbreaks, outages, outpatients). Related 'external/outside/foreign' words fire moderately.

Fires on prepositions and an opening parenthesis that come right after a verb or noun and introduce a complement or aside: 'halt by', 'appointed by', 'ban for', 'founder in', 'Copyright (', 'increase (P less than'. The links between these cases are loose.

Mixed: fires on specific tokens of recurring named entities and code boilerplate, such as 'Latter' in Latter-day Saints, Hamas/Palestinians, '@implementation' in Objective-C, '/local' in /usr/local, 'maxcdn', '$GLOBALS', and capitalized license words (PROFITS, FITNESS). No shared meaning.

Fires on the word after a verb of beginning, origin or transition in historical or narrative text, especially before a date ('founded in 1965', 'opened in 1847', 'since its inception', 'since the dawn of', 'parted ways', 'fallen into', 'set out', 'wake up to'). It tracks phrases about when or how something started or changed state.

Fires on directional or aspectual particles and prepositions that complete a verb of motion or continuation ('keeps on', 'passing over/through', 'falls below', 'come out', 'walked towards', 'takes on'). There are also unrelated strong hits on code whitespace/indentation and ':=' tokens.

A mixture: subword fragments of Latin taxonomic and chemical names (Euglena grac|ilis, cyclo|hex, Gr|ac|ilibacillus), 'https' in markdown links, code indentation, French function words, and assorted proper-name fragments. No common thread.

A mixture: broken unicode or special-character tokens (non-breaking-space bytes before 'years', '.degree'), header and license boilerplate tokens (Microsoft, OpenSSL, LICENSE, '*****', '~~~~'), and an assortment of names and technical terms near the start of documents. No single concept.

Fires mainly on word-initial 'ex'/'ass'/'ins'/'inter' prefix fragments starting a split Latinate word (ex|ploderede, EX|POSE, Ex|plain, ex|amination, Ass|istant, ass|ayed, Ins|pections), plus some byte fragments of non-Latin scripts. The common feature is the first piece of a word broken after its prefix.

Fires on the pronoun 'it' (and 'It', Danish 'Det'), most strongly at the start of a clause after a conjunction or connective ('And it', 'so it', 'as it turned out', 'if it', 'Then it'). Sentence-initial 'It' after a period, or object 'it', fires more weakly.
